Question:
In the table shown, the formula relating \(x\) and \(y\) is:

\[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5\\ \hline y & 3 & 7 & 13 & 21 & 31\\ \hline\end{array}\]
Solution:
Compare each listed \(y\)-value with the square of its corresponding \(x\)-value. The differences are
\[
3-1=2,\quad 7-4=3,\quad 13-9=4,\quad
21-16=5,\quad 31-25=6.
\]
These differences are exactly \(x+1\), suggesting \(y=x^2+x+1\). Substituting all five inputs confirms that this formula gives
\[
3,\ 7,\ 13,\ 21,\ 31,
\]
exactly the displayed outputs.

To check uniqueness among the choices, A gives \(11\), rather than \(13\), at \(x=3\). B gives \(8\), rather than \(7\), at \(x=2\). D gives \(0\), rather than \(3\), at \(x=1\). Since C fits every entry, E does not apply.

Thus the matching listed formula is \(\boxed{y=x^2+x+1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
